title: Con tal de que + subjuntivo: una condición explícita

sections.content: Con tal de que (provided that, as long as) states an explicit condition attached to an offer or a tolerance -- exactly the shape of US Cold War policy, which backed reform and aid on the condition that a government stayed anti-communist. It always takes the subjunctive. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: Kennedy lanzó la Alianza para el Progreso, con tal de que los países receptores emprendieran reformas moderadas capaces de reducir la desigualdad.
items.english: Kennedy launched the Alliance for Progress, provided that recipient countries undertook moderate reforms capable of reducing inequality.

items.spanish: Estados Unidos estaba dispuesto a comprometer miles de millones de dólares, con tal de que los gobiernos aceptaran alinearse con el bloque occidental.
items.english: The United States was willing to commit billions of dollars, provided that governments agreed to align with the Western bloc.

items.spanish: Algunos países implementaron reformas reales con tal de que continuara llegando la ayuda estadounidense.
items.english: Some countries implemented real reforms so that American aid would keep coming.

items.spanish: Washington estaba dispuesto a tolerar prácticamente cualquier cosa, con tal de que un gobierno se mantuviera firmemente alineado contra el comunismo.
items.english: Washington was willing to tolerate practically anything, as long as a government stayed firmly aligned against communism.

sections.content: Con tal de + infinitive (same subject) is the shorter alternative when the person setting the condition and the person meeting it are the same -- lo hizo con tal de conseguir la ayuda -- while con tal de que + subjunctive is for two different subjects, as in every example above.
